Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 50
  gender: Female
  ethnicity: South Asian
  relationship_status: Single
  occupation: Diplomat
  trauma_type: Toxic chemical exposure
  pcl5: 34

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Stressors: avoid anything that could be stressful, Magical Thinking: I tell myself the event did not really happen or was not that bad, Avoid Thinking: Thinking about the event
  Threat: Irritability: Irritable behavior, angry outbursts, or acting aggressively, Body on Alert: My body feels constantly tense and ready to react to danger, Scanning for Danger: I constantly scan my surroundings for signs of danger
  Memory: Triggered Without Warning: Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning, Cannot Explain Clearly: When I try to explain what happened I lose the thread and cannot finish, Taste Vividness: I can taste what I tasted during the event when the memory returns

Vignette:
As a seasoned diplomat, Rohini had grown accustomed to navigating high-stakes situations with poise and precision. But nothing could have prepared her for the day she was exposed to toxic chemicals during a meeting at a foreign embassy. The memory of that event still felt like an open wound, one that she struggled to confront even two years later. Rohini's recollection of the incident was fragmented, but certain details stood out with vivid clarity. She remembered the taste of metal in her mouth, the acrid smell of burning wires, and the sound of alarms blaring as people scrambled to evacuate the room. What frightened her most was the feeling of losing control, of being unable to escape the suffocating cloud of noxious fumes that seemed to seep into every pore. In the aftermath of the incident, Rohini began to notice a growing sense of irritability. She found herself snapping at colleagues and friends for no reason, her anger simmering just below the surface like a pot about to boil over. Her body felt constantly tense, as if she was perpetually poised on the edge of flight or fight. At night, she would lie awake, scanning her surroundings for signs of danger, convinced that some new threat lurked just beyond the shadows. Rohini tried to avoid anything that could be stressful, hoping to escape the anxiety that had become her constant companion. She began to turn down high-profile assignments, citing "diplomatic fatigue" as a convenient excuse. But this strategy only seemed to make things worse, as she felt increasingly disconnected from the work that had once given her such purpose and meaning. As the months dragged on, Rohini's avoidance behaviors became more entrenched. She stopped attending social gatherings, fearful of being confronted with situations or people that might trigger memories of the event. When friends or family asked about her experience, she would launch into a vague narrative, only to trail off mid-sentence as if losing the thread. It was as if she couldn't quite bring herself to confront the reality of what had happened. Rohini's attempt to downplay the severity of the incident had become a sort of magical thinking. She told herself that it wasn't really that bad, that she was overreacting to a minor scare. But deep down, she knew this wasn't true. The memories still lingered, vivid and alive, waiting to pounce on her at any moment. One day, while walking through a crowded market, Rohini caught a whiff of something that instantly transported her back to the embassy. The taste of metal flooded her mouth once more, and she felt herself spiraling into a panic. It was as if no time had passed at all, and she was right back in the midst of that toxic nightmare. This latest episode marked a turning point for Rohini. She realized that she couldn't keep running from her memories, or trying to convince herself that they weren't real. The stress of living with PTSD had begun to take a toll on her relationships and her work, and she knew it was time to seek help. As she sat in the therapist's office, she felt a mix of emotions: fear, hope, and above all, a deep longing to reclaim her life from the grip of trauma.
